subject: Executive signoff needed — Helios Labs renewal: tailored make-right + SLA amendment
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@helioslabs.com>, Tom Porter <tporter@helioslabs.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2029 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Helios Labs renewal — one-time preservation package & SLA addendum

Team / Alyssa, Tom —

Quick background: Helios Labs (bioinformatics pipelines) is up for renewal on 2029-08-01. They flagged a competitive RFP and are specifically asking for better uptime guarantees + longer log retention to satisfy clinical audit needs. They are a strategic healthcare account (~$1.2M ARR) with significant expansion potential in 2030 if we retain them.

Current ask (what I'm proposing we present as a limited one-time offer to win):
- 20% discount on year-1 committed spend (applies to base subscription only)
- $150k one-time credit to offset migration/perf remediation costs (applied as invoice credit)
- Term reset to 24 months (from current 12) to lock in renewal
- SLA addendum: HIPAA-aligned incident response, 99.9% availability commitment, extended audit-log retention to 13 months (instead of default 6)

Rationale: Helios reports a spike in token usage and has been impacted by two transient latencys during Q2. Competitor X is offering a 15% discount + SLA language; without a stronger preservation offer they will likely flip. I believe this is a one-time preservation concession that protects the long-term expansion path (we expect +$600k in net-new ARR over the next 12–18 months if retained).

Requesting: Deal-desk and executive signoff on the package above. Need legal to vet the SLA wording, and finance to sign off on the $150k credit impact. If approved, I will attach to the renewal signature package and request Helios sign by 2029-07-25 to make the timeline.

Attachments: Helios_Renewal_Summary_20290717.pdf (usage & pricing), Helios_usage_snapshot_Q2.csv

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Request: Helios Labs renewal — one-time preservation package & SLA addendum

Vanessa —

Thanks for the write-up. A few clarifying points we need before we can escalate for exec approval: 
1) Net ARR impact: please confirm the expected net retention ARR if we grant the package vs. churn scenario (dollarized).
2) Credit mechanics: is the $150k a one-time invoice credit or spread across invoices? Impact to recognized revenue and timing matters for finance.
3) SLA language: legal will need a specific draft for "HIPAA-aligned incident response" and exact SLO metrics (MTTR buckets, service credits formula). I assume we mean standard service credits up to X% of monthly fees — please specify.
4) Alternate offers: can we model a scaled credit (e.g., $100k) with a slightly higher discount (25% Y1) and an adoption milestone to limit downside?

Please respond with the dollarized scenario and an annotated SLA draft. Once we have that, I'll circulate to finance/legal and include a recommended approval threshold.

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Deal Desk Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Wed, 17 Jul 2029 09:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Helios Labs renewal — one-time preservation package & SLA addendum

Rishi —

Answered inline and attached a short risk / ROI packet (Helios_Risk_Rating.xlsx):
1) Net ARR impact: If we retain with the package, expected retained ARR = $1.2M (base) + projected expansions ~ $600k over 12–18 months = $1.8M. If we lose the account, worst-case churn = full $1.2M ARR; mid case partial migration = ~60% ($720k). So the delta versus churn is $1.2M retained at-risk.
2) Credit mechanics: propose one-time invoice credit applied at next statement (not revenue-recognized as revenue; it's contra-revenue in finance model). Finance estimate of P&L impact in year-1 = $150k reduction in recognized ARR for accounting period of application.
3) SLA language (summary): propose a 99.9% monthly availability SLO with service credits capped at 50% of monthly fees for qualifying incidents; dedicated incident response contact within 1 hour and enhanced post-incident reports; audit-log retention extended to 13 months via a managed cold-store export. I'm attaching a redline-ready SLA summary we can hand to legal.
4) Alternate modeled offer: $100k credit + 25% Y1 discount + 18-month term reset + retention milestone (if usage recovers by 20% QoQ we extend credits to support onboarding). This lowers near-term cash impact but is less attractive to Helios.

Why this matters: Helios is embedded in two of their clinical pipelines used for revenue-generating analytics. Competitor messaging is strong on uptime guarantees; losing them would create immediate revenue loss and reduce credibility with other healthcare prospects. This is a high-risk, high-reward decision where a measured make-right preserves a strategic anchor account.

Requested next steps: Rishi, please route to finance/legal with the attachments. Jonas/Marissa — endorsement and one-line exec signoff ("approve limited package as proposed, valid until 2029-07-25") would get this to the customer in time.

Attachments: Helios_Risk_Rating.xlsx

Thanks —
Vanessa
